node.label: Peter Burke
node.date_label: Popular Culture in Early Modern Europe (1978) · The French Historical Revolution: The Annales School, 1929–89 (1990) · What is Cultural History? (2004)
node.description: A cultural historian of early modern Europe who also writes about historical methods and the history of knowledge. His selected historiographical essay resists describing cultural history as a simple sequence in which each approach displaces the last. In a 2022 interview, he explains how Popular Culture combined wide comparison with attention to regional variation and discusses how changing scale alters historical explanation. The interview also insists on multiple historical voices, connecting structures with individual experience rather than choosing one for every inquiry.

proposed_edges.relationship: Questions a simple replacement model of cultural approaches while investigating historical meanings and cultural variation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Reuse of the existing essay reading, PDF pp. 1–13 and selected opening of p. 14. The arrow adopts its limited anti-succession argument, not all of Burke’s survey or a verified genealogy for every predecessor.

proposed_edges.relationship: Explains how changes in research scale alter plausible explanations, linking regional cultural variation with wider comparisons.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Primary interview, question 7, read. Burke discusses the scale question and describes his own popular-culture research; this is a methodological contribution, not membership in one microhistorical school or a claim that he invented scale analysis.
